body:
# Independent audit of local common-arc polygonization

Audited `candidate 3bf99e512cb9551a`.

The local theorem passes under its stated finite-gap, common-homothety, and
constant-cap-membership hypotheses. No global classification follows.

1. A precise outer construction is the intersection of all original support
   halfplanes with normals outside the interior of I and finitely many chosen
   original support halfplanes within I. It contains K, has exactly the
   original support function outside int(I), and has a polygonal boundary
   inside I. Its endpoint facets are permissible. Dense normals give
   Hausdorff convergence.
2. The inner construction is the convex hull of the unchanged complementary
   boundary and finitely many increasingly dense points of the chosen arc.
   It is contained in K and has the same outside support function. Each
   support point with an outside normal was retained. Dense points give
   Hausdorff convergence.
3. The support functions of the two bodies agree with the original one
   outside int(I). Therefore their Minkowski interpolation does too. The
   outside one-sided boundary limits, and hence the fixed endpoints of the
   replaced arc, do not move. Inside I only finitely many edge-normal angles
   occur, even after interpolation. All interpolants have polygonal arcs.
4. Their total areas bracket |K|; continuity gives an interpolant of exact
   area |K|. Since the complementary boundary is unchanged, this is exactly
   preservation of the signed area relative to the fixed endpoint chord.
5. Simultaneous homotheties and translations multiply each area difference
   by c_z^2. Translation cross terms vanish because the support difference
   is zero at both endpoint angles. The global H^1 support formula for area
   handles endpoint curvature atoms without omitting their contribution.
6. With finitely many caps and fibers, positive separation of every affected
   compact arc from every relevant cap boundary has a uniform positive
   minimum. For sufficiently close replacements the changed regions retain
   exactly the indicated cap memberships. Each cap-area change is either
   zero or the entire fiber-area change, and hence is zero.
7. Coefficientwise equal support relations remain exact. A finite family of
   remaining relations with a uniform positive gap on I survives a uniformly
   small support change. Nothing changes outside I.

A minor useful wrapper: if the common h is originally only a function on I,
choose a fiber with c_z>0 and extend h globally as that fiber's translated
and rescaled support function. This supplies the base convex body required
by the single-arc lemma. If all c_z vanish, the proposed replacement is
vacuous.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
